# CoverSlide

The deck's cover: title, subheader and meta at the top left, the deck's registered cover art on Cream, and the logo in a solid Navy badge flush to the bottom-right corner. The cover has no footer strip; the badge takes its place.

Fixed slides are the same in every deck. Build them from this card exactly; don't improvise them from a layout.

## Anatomy

| Part | Set | Place |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Light 300, 81px, line height 0.9, ALL CAPS, Navy | left `m-edge`, top 88px, 1040px wide at most |
| Subheader | Light 300, 31px, line height 1.16, sentence case | 26px below the title, 900px wide at most |
| Month | Regular 400, 24px, ALL CAPS, −0.01em, `orange-700` | 34px below the subheader |
| Presenter | Regular 400, 24px, line height 1.3 | the line under the month |
| Art | the deck's cover, from the table below | behind the type block and the badge |
| Badge | Navy box, padding 46 / 80 / 60 / 64px, White logo 300px wide | flush bottom-right |

The month in Orange 700 measures about 2.5:1 on Cream, below the 3:1 floor for large text; it stays because the source sets it, as one of the sanctioned orange moments.

## Covers

The frame never changes. Each deck picks one art layer for it, once.

| Cover | Art | Placement |
|---|---|---|
| `mountain` | `WPPOpen_Mountain-01.png` | full-bleed; the locked default |
| `crystal` | `WPPOpen_Crystal-01.png` | right-anchored |
| `coral` | `WPPOpen_Coral-01.png` | right-anchored |
| `dots` | the `cover-dots` preset | tone-on-tone White, Orange 500 and Orange 600 dots on Cream, no image |
| `playbook` | the `cover-playbook` preset | pure type on Cream with an Orange 600 drift off the top right, no image |

Right-anchored art is 1440px wide, vertically centred, and hangs 140px off the right edge.

## What the consumer supplies

A short title, two to four words in capitals; a subheader of one sentence; the month and year; and the presenter.

## In Claude Design Slides

For `mountain`, `crystal` or `coral`, copy the cover's art and `WPP_ES_MAP_logo_WHITE.svg` from this system into the deck first.

```html
<section id="cover" style="background:#FAFAF0; color:#000050; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif">
  <img src="/_blob/<mountain-id>" alt="" style="position:absolute; left:0px; top:0px; width:1920px; height:1080px; object-fit:cover">
  <div style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:88px; width:1040px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:34px">
    <div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:26px">
      <h1 style="font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:81px; line-height:0.9; text-transform:uppercase">Deck title in capitals</h1>
      <p style="max-width:900px; font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:31px; line-height:1.16">One line that says what the deck is for</p>
    </div>
    <div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column">
      <p style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; line-height:1.3; letter-spacing:-0.01em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#FF7800">September 2026</p>
      <p style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; line-height:1.3">[Presenter name]</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="position:absolute; right:0px; bottom:0px; background:#000050; padding:46px 80px 60px 64px">
    <img src="/_blob/<logo-id>" alt="WPP Enterprise Solutions | MAP" style="width:300px; height:40px; object-fit:contain">
  </div>
</section>
```

Use the full-bleed art in Slides, crystal and coral too: the right-anchored version hangs 140px off the canvas, which a slide's pinned boxes cannot do. The logo is 300 × 40px at its own proportions.

## In the HTML deck

`.slide.cover-mountain` with `.cover-mountain__head` and `.cover-mountain__badge`; the art is `.cover-art--full` (mountain), `.cover-art--right` (crystal, coral) or `.cover-dots` carrying the `cover-dots` or `cover-playbook` preset. The cover is the spec's `cover`.

# AgendaSlide

The agenda: the headline at the top left, then one row per chapter, each an Orange 700 numeral in WPP Thin beside the chapter name in WPP Light, and the agenda's dot cluster in the top-right corner. Cream ground, with the footer strip.

Fixed slides are the same in every deck. Build them from this card exactly; don't improvise them from a layout.

## Anatomy

| Part | Set | Place |
|---|---|---|
| Headline | Light 300, 54px, line height 1.02 | left `m-edge`, top 112px |
| Rows | one per chapter | left `m-edge`; the first row's top at y = 266px, one row every 148px |
| Numeral | Thin 100, 88px, −0.02em, `orange-700`, written "1." | a 118px column, 44px before the name |
| Chapter | Light 300, 50px, Navy, sentence case | numeral and name share a baseline |
| Dense variant | numeral 72px in a 98px column, chapter 42px | for an agenda of 6 chapters; the first row's top at y = 224px, one row every 128px |
| Dots | the `agenda` preset: Orange 700, 600 and 800 | top-right, cropped by the edges |

The agenda is one of two compositions allowed a multi-colour dot scatter; the classic divider is the other (the default divider is one hue). The numerals in Orange 700 on Cream measure about 2.5:1; at 88px Thin the system treats them as wayfinding-scale type, as it does for large KPI numerals.

## What the consumer supplies

The chapter names, three to five for the standard variant (six take the dense one), and the headline if it isn't "Agenda". Six chapters is the most: split a longer deck. Keep each name within about 45 characters, or its row runs under the dots.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<section id="agenda" style="background:#FAFAF0; color:#000050; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif">
  <svg aria-label="" width="1920" height="1080" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" style="position:absolute; left:0px; top:0px; width:1920px; height:1080px">
    <circle cx="1880" cy="50" r="180" fill="#FF7800"/>
    <circle cx="1645" cy="375" r="75" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
    <circle cx="1560" cy="210" r="40" fill="#D94E0E"/>
  </svg>
  <h2 style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:112px; width:1300px; font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:54px; line-height:1.02; letter-spacing:-0.005em">Agenda</h2>
  <div style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:266px; width:1300px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:60px">
    <div style="display:flex; flex-direction:row; align-items:baseline; gap:44px">
      <p style="width:118px; flex:none; font-family:'WPP Thin', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:88px; line-height:1; letter-spacing:-0.02em; color:#FF7800">1.</p>
      <p style="font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:50px; line-height:1">Where we are today</p>
    </div>
    <!-- one row per chapter -->
  </div>
  <!-- footer strip: see FooterFurniture -->
</section>
```

Each row is as tall as its 88px numeral, so the 60px gap puts the rows 148px apart. For the dense variant set the numerals to 72px in a 98px column and the names to 42px, start at `top:224px` and use `gap:56px`.

## In the HTML deck

`.slide.agenda` (`.agenda--dense`), with `.toc-row`, `.n`, `.t` and the `agenda` dot preset.

# DividerSlide

The chapter divider, in the playbook composition: macro and mid dots in the deck's one divider hue across the top and right, the chapter number at the top left, and the chapter title in WPP Thin capitals at 136px, pinned low at the bottom left with its sub-label above it. It keeps the brand line and page number.

Fixed slides are the same in every deck. Build them from this card exactly; don't improvise them from a layout. Every divider in a deck is identical: only the number, title and sub-label change.

## Anatomy

| Part | Set | Place |
|---|---|---|
| Number | Thin 100, 104px, line height 1, −0.02em, written `01.` | left `m-edge`, top 56px |
| Sub-label | Medium 500, 22px, +0.14em, ALL CAPS, `orange-800` (`orange-600` on `navy-full`), written `Section 1` | directly above the title, 26px gap |
| Title | Thin 100, 136px, line height 0.88, −0.02em, ALL CAPS, lines balanced | left `m-edge`, 96px above the bottom, 1560px wide at most |
| Dots | the `divider-playbook` preset: seven circles, all in the colourway's one hue | top and right, bleeding off at least two edges, one fused pair |

The title may overlap the dots: display type over flat dots is sanctioned on dividers. No dot enters the number's top-left zone or the title's bottom-left zone, and the large bottom-right dot is placed so the footer stays legible in every colourway.

## Colourways

Each deck picks one colourway, and every divider in it uses it. The deck's direction sets the default: `orange` for editorial-quiet and data-forward, `navy-dots` for statement-led, `navy-full` for high-impact.

| Colourway | Ground | Type | Sub-label | Dots | Brand line and page number | Confidential line | Classic second dot | Classic third dot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `orange` | `#FAFAF0` | `#000050` | `#D94E0E` | `#FF7800` | `#000050` | `#000050` | `#F9BD5D` | `#D94E0E` |
| `orange-600` | `#FAFAF0` | `#000050` | `#D94E0E` | `#F9BD5D` | `#000050` | `#000050` | `#FF7800` | `#D94E0E` |
| `orange-500` | `#FAFAF0` | `#000050` | `#D94E0E` | `#FFF5CD` | `#000050` | `#000050` | `#F9BD5D` | `#FF7800` |
| `white` | `#FAFAF0` | `#000050` | `#D94E0E` | `#FFFFFF` | `#000050` | `#000050` | `#FFFFFF` | `#FFF5CD` |
| `navy-dots` | `#FAFAF0` | `#000050` | `#D94E0E` | `#000050` | `#FFFFFF` | `#000050` | `#000050` | `#FF7800` |
| `navy-full` | `#000050` | `#FFFFFF` | `#F9BD5D` | `#FAFAF0` | `#000050` | `#FFFFFF` | `#FFFFFF` | `#FF7800` |

On `navy-dots` the brand line and page number turn White because they sit on the navy bottom-right dot; on `navy-full` they turn Navy because they sit on its Cream dot. The sub-label in Orange 800 on Cream measures about 4:1, below the 4.5:1 floor for 22px text; it stays because the source sets it.

## The classic variant

`dividerStyle: "classic"` keeps the older v3 geometry as a registered variant, in the same colourways: the number top-left, a 104px title (line height 0.86) 214px above the bottom, the sub-label below it at left 84px and 150px above the bottom, and four right-anchored macro dots (Ø 760, 560, 180 and 90px) in the colourway's dot colour and its two classic dot colours from the table. Use it only when the deck asks for it.

## What the consumer supplies

The chapter number and a short chapter title, two lines at most. The sub-label is `Section 1`, `Section 2` and so on (`Sección N` in Spanish decks).

## In Claude Design Slides

The `orange` colourway; for another, swap the colours from the table.

```html
  <svg aria-label="" width="1920" height="1080" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" style="position:absolute; left:0px; top:0px; width:1920px; height:1080px">
    <circle cx="850" cy="30" r="150" fill="#FF7800"/>
    <circle cx="1030" cy="40" r="100" fill="#FF7800"/>
    <circle cx="1700" cy="100" r="340" fill="#FF7800"/>
    <circle cx="1870" cy="450" r="210" fill="#FF7800"/>
    <circle cx="1330" cy="270" r="90" fill="#FF7800"/>
    <circle cx="1780" cy="1020" r="280" fill="#FF7800"/>
    <circle cx="1195" cy="475" r="45" fill="#FF7800"/>
  </svg>
  <p style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:56px; width:600px; font-family:'WPP Thin', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:104px; line-height:1; letter-spacing:-0.02em">01.</p>
  <div style="position:absolute; left:40px; bottom:96px; width:1560px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:26px">
    <p style="font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:22px; letter-spacing:0.14em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#D94E0E">Section 1</p>
    <h2 style="font-family:'WPP Thin', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:136px; line-height:0.88; letter-spacing:-0.02em; text-transform:uppercase">Where we are today</h2>
  </div>
  <!-- brand line and page number: see FooterFurniture, in the colourway's colour -->
</section>
```

The dot `<svg>` comes first so the title paints over it. Slides cannot balance lines automatically, so break a two-line title by hand with `<br>` to keep the lines close in length.

## In the HTML deck

`.slide.divider` (with `.slide--navy` on `navy-full`), `.dv-num` and `.dv-block` holding `.dv-sub` and `.dv-title`, and the `divider-playbook` dot preset; the colourway is the spec's `dividerColourway`.

# ThankYouSlide

The outro: "Thank you." in WPP Light at 99px, contact lines beneath it, and the outro's dots bleeding off the right edge, with the footer strip. Two outros ship: light, the default, and dark.

Fixed slides are the same in every deck. Build them from this card exactly; don't improvise them from a layout.

## Anatomy

| Part | Set | Place |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Light 300, 99px, line height 0.9, sentence case | left `m-edge`, top 430px |
| Contact | Regular 400, 24px, line height 1.5, one line each | left `m-edge`, top 580px |
| Dots | the `thankyou` preset, in the outro's three dot colours | right edge and bottom-right corner |

## Outros

Each deck picks one outro. Light is the default; the high-impact direction suggests dark.

| Outro | Ground | Type | Dots | Brand line and page number | Confidential line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `light` | `#FAFAF0` | `#000050` | `#FF7800` · `#F9BD5D` · `#D94E0E` | `#000050` | `#000050` |
| `dark` | `#000050` | `#FFFFFF` | `#FAFAF0` · `#FFFFFF` · `#FF7800` | `#000050` | `#FFFFFF` |

The three dot colours are the macro, mid and small dot, in that order. On the dark outro the brand line and page number stay Navy because they sit on its big Cream dot, and the confidential line, on the Navy ground, turns White.

## What the consumer supplies

The contact lines, optional: name, role and email, or the team's shared address. Without them the slide closes on the words alone. Spanish decks close on “Gracias.”

## In Claude Design Slides

The light outro:

```html
<section id="thank-you" style="background:#FAFAF0; color:#000050; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif">
  <svg aria-label="" width="1920" height="1080" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" style="position:absolute; left:0px; top:0px; width:1920px; height:1080px">
    <circle cx="1880" cy="1000" r="380" fill="#FF7800"/>
    <circle cx="1790" cy="30" r="150" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
    <circle cx="1435" cy="835" r="75" fill="#D94E0E"/>
  </svg>
  <h2 style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:430px; width:1200px; font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:99px; line-height:0.9">Thank you.</h2>
  <div style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:580px; width:1200px; display:flex; flex-direction:column">
    <p style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; line-height:1.5">[Name Surname]</p>
    <p style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; line-height:1.5">[name.surname@wpp.com]</p>
  </div>
  <!-- footer strip: see FooterFurniture -->
</section>
```

For the dark outro, set the section's `background:#000050; color:#FFFFFF`, fill the same three circles `#FAFAF0`, `#FFFFFF` and `#FF7800` in that order, and set the brand line and page number in `#000050` and the confidential line in `#FFFFFF`.

## In the HTML deck

`.slide.thank-you` (with `.slide--navy` on the dark outro), `.ty`, `.ty-contact` and the `thankyou` dot preset; the outro is the spec's `outro`.
